free_tier.stated: Free tier reported as 5 NZB downloads and 25 API hits per day, no XXX access; Basic EUR 10/year gives 5,000 API hits and unlimited downloads, Pro EUR 20/year 20,000, Elite EUR 35/year unlimited plus Spotweb. The vendor's own caps declares <limits max="100" default="100"/> and <registration available="yes" open="yes"/>.
free_tier.notes: Two 2026 third-party tables agree on 5 downloads / 25 API per day; a 2013 vendor forum post said 10 API and 5 downloads, and a March 2020 promotion raised it temporarily to 250 API and 100 downloads. The conservative 25 is kept.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: an NZB pointer file

retention.stated: '18+ years of posts in our DB' (login page strapline); a third-party listing claims 'over 3,600 days of binary content, 500,000+ NZBs indexed'.
retention.notes: The vendor states a span in years, not a day count; the day figure is third-party.

egress.terms: No byte metering; the API returns pointers.

interface_detail: Newznab API on the same host at /api. caps advertises 100 results per request and open registration. The site lists Sonarr, Radarr, Prowlarr, NZBHydra 2, SickChill/SickGear, Chaptarr, Mylar, Lazylibrarian and Lidarr as compatible.
tooling: Native Newznab, no wrapper: Prowlarr, NZBHydra2 and every arr app add it with URL plus key.
chaining: An open-registration indexer with a real API key on the free tier, so it can carry an arr stack at 25 searches and 5 grabs a day before EUR 10/year lifts the ceiling.

limits.value: 25 API hits per day and 5 NZB downloads per day on the free tier

limits_note: Registration is declared open today, which is the one difference that matters against every other invite-only indexer.
binding_note: At a 1 TiB/month habit the daily counter is what stops a user: 25 API hits a day is roughly one search per hour, and the 5-grab cap allows about 50 GB a day at a 10 GB average NZB, which is 1.5 TB a month only if nothing retries.

identity_cost.detail: Registration declares itself open in caps and /register serves an email field with the warning 'Temporary e-mail domains are banned', plus a verification link. Spam-blocking is the gate, not an invite.

reliability_note: Free accounts have been re-capped before without notice (the 2013 status post reverted a temporary lift), so a free allowance is a policy number that can change under a running stack.
confidence_note: caps and the open-registration flag were measured; the free allowance that decides the verdict is third-party. One free account would settle it and would move the record to documented.
